MRI_source_pixels.caption:
Read labels at full sizePeroneus quartus is present in this source variant example. Panel a is axial fat-suppressed proton-density FSE MRI; blue, green and red arrows identify peroneus brevis, peroneus longus and peroneus quartus, with yellow arrows marking the accessory belly. Coronal T1 FSE b and sagittal T1 FSE c show its visible descent toward the calcaneus. Side and individual clinical status are unreported; this example does not establish a complete course or attachment footprint.
Identified in this figure: Peroneus quartus (source-labelled accessory belly and limited visible descent); Peroneus brevis (source-labelled local axial appearance); Peroneus longus (source-labelled local axial appearance).
Source-labelled peroneus quartus variant in three published sections. No side, individual age/sex, complete exam findings or global normality is supplied. The study uses 1.5 T MRI, but this figure has no DICOM metadata or exact panel-specific acquisition provenance. The 760×331 repository JPEG cannot establish a full musculotendinous course, attachment footprint, tissue dimensions, dynamic crowding or symptom causation; no 3D reconstruction is supported. The caption specifies a distal direction toward the retrotrochlear eminence, which is not equivalent to a validated attachment footprint. Its case-specific location is not a universal origin/insertion pattern. No accessory soleus or FDAL is illustrated.

Read labels at full sizeOne source-depicted peroneus-quartus pattern alongside the usual brevis/longus tendons. It is a teaching course illustration, not a measured subject or a universal origin/insertion map.
Identified in this figure: Peroneus quartus: source-depicted local course; Peroneus brevis; Peroneus longus; Retrotrochlear eminence of calcaneus.
One source-described PQ pattern only. Other origins and insertions occur; no measured tissue dimensions, complete individual attachment footprint, dynamic compression or 3D volume is supplied.
